The Unicode-name listings of MAM for Sefaria

Author: Ben Denckla

Revision: 2026-10-26

Introduction

The folder misc/unicode-names/ of MAM-for-Sefaria lists, by their Unicode names, the code points of the verses of the folder csv/, whose files the page The encoding of MAM for Sefaria describes. This page describes the listings. Every count and example on it is taken from the files.

This page has two typographic conventions:

  1. Text styled like this reveals more on hover, where the medium allows hovering.
  2. ZARQA is the name of a Unicode code point, less the words that name its script and class. Hovering shows the whole name, here HEBREW ACCENT ZARQA.

The listings

The folder has a listing for each file of csv/, named as that file is but for its extension, as I Samuel.txt is, and a provenance note, _provenance.md. The listings are text files in UTF-8, with LF line ends. A listing's first line is unicode_names Genesis, for its book. Then each verse has a line that names it, a line for each run of its text, and a blank line, but for the last verse.

The line that names a verse has the book's identifier in MAM-basics, the chapter and verse, and the verse numbering, which is Sefaria's, as Genesis 1:5 in vtrad vtsef and Levit 1:1 in vtrad vtsef do. Each SPACE and NO-BREAK SPACE has a line of its own, with its name, and so splits the text into runs. A run's line has its code points, separated by commas, each by the short name that the table below gives it. Each HTML element has lines of its own: one with START and the element's tag and class before its contents, and one with STOP after them, or a single line with START/STOP for br, which has no contents.

For example, Gen 1:5 has this text in csv/:

וַיִּקְרָ֨א אֱלֹהִ֤ים ׀ לָאוֹר֙ י֔וֹם וְלַחֹ֖שֶׁךְ קָ֣רָא לָ֑יְלָה וַֽיְהִי־עֶ֥רֶב וַֽיְהִי־בֹ֖קֶר י֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃ {פ}
